definitions.explanation: Showing a striking difference when compared. Used to describe two things that are markedly different from each other.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{性格|せいかく}は{対照的|たいしょうてき}だ。
{姉|あね}と{妹|いもうと}は{対照的|たいしょうてき}な{生|い}き{方|かた}をしている。
examples.english: The older and younger sisters lead contrasting lifestyles.

examples.japanese: {都会|とかい}の{喧騒|けんそう}と{対照的|たいしょうてき}に、この{村|むら}は{静|しず}かで{穏|おだ}やかだ。
examples.english: In contrast to the hustle and bustle of the city, this village is quiet and peaceful.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{対照的|たいしょうてき} can be used as a na-adjective modifier ({対照的|たいしょうてき}な) or with に as an adverb ({対照的|たいしょうてき}に, meaning "in contrast"). It often appears in the pattern AとBは{対照的|たいしょうてき}だ (A and B are contrasting).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対照的|たいしょうてき}な{性格|せいかく} — contrasting personalities
- Xと{対照的|たいしょうてき}に — in contrast to X
- {対照的|たいしょうてき}な{結果|けっか} — contrasting results
- きわめて{対照的|たいしょうてき}だ — to be in stark contrast

SIMILAR WORDS:
The base noun {対照|たいしょう} means contrast or comparison. {対比|たいひ} also means contrast but is used as a noun/suru verb. {正反対|せいはんたい} means the exact opposite, which is stronger than {対照的|たいしょうてき}.
